newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold ends with pared gains, bullion sags.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold ends with pared gains, bullion sags.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based gold futures ended firmer on Wednesday, but off life-of-contract highs hit early in the session, taking its cues from the forex market where the yen opened lower against the dollar but then bounced back.

Bullion prices, by contrast, dipped slightly in quiet trade, pressured by light Swiss selling after an overnight probe of the upside failed to break through a band of resistance at $380.50 to $382.00 an ounce, traders said.
TOCOM most-active August 1997 gold ended four yen higher at 1,349 yen per gram, off its early peak of 1,354, the contract's highest ever and a three-month high for a most-active contract.
Bullion closed at $380.80/$381.10, off slightly from New York's closing quote of $381.10/60.

Individual investors continued to liquidate long positions in the TOCOM December gold contract this morning. Further liquidation was expected in the weeks ahead and this could weigh on the market, traders said.
Today's activity was light, however, ahead of the Sports Day holiday in Japan on Thursday.
Other precious metals ended narrowly mixed, receiving little direction from quiet bullion markets and showing only a muted reaction to activity in the currencies.
Most-active August 1997 platinum settled one yen firmer at 1,366 yen per gram, while the other months were two lower to three higher.
August 1997 palladium settled one yen lower at 424 yen per gram while August 1997 silver was off 0.2 yen at 177.7 yen per 10 grams.
